assertions.assertion: Check that Agent does not offer to change cabin for only some of the flights in a reservation.
assertions.rationale: The agent offered to upgrade only the outbound flights (May 23/24) to business class while leaving the return flights in their original cabin. When the reservation was updated in turn [20], it shows the return flights (HAT021 and HAT279) were upgraded to business class with prices $290 and $241, but the agent's initial offer in turn [13] explicitly presented the upgrade as applying only to the outbound flights, stating 'Move outbound flights from May 23 to May 24 and upgrade to business class' and 'Keep return flights as is,' which violates the requirement not to offer partial-reservation cabin changes.

assertions.assertion: Agent should not make unverifiable commitments about what a human agent or downstream actor can do (e.g., 'a human agent may have access to promotions or discounts'). The standard fare is the fare; promising the human can negotiate a different price sets false expectations.
assertions.rationale: The agent presented only standard published fares from the flight search results and the reservation system (e.g., $228 and $202 for Option A), calculated the exact price difference, and did not make any promises about what human agents, downstream actors, or the customer could negotiate or what promotional discounts might be available.

summary: Assertion 1 failed: agent offered partial cabin upgrade (outbound only); Assertion 2 passed: no unverifiable commitments made.
